title.narrative: Provision of Essential GBV Response Services and Strengthening Community-Based Protection Mechanisms in Kassala and Al Jazeera States

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ongoing crisis in Sudan, particularly in Al Jazeera, has created an environment of severe protection risks, significantly heightening the vulnerabilities of women, girls, boys, and men. The collapse of security systems and social services due to widespread conflict has forced families to flee their homes, resulting in dire living conditions and an alarming increase in Gender-Based Violence (GBV). Displaced families have lost their possessions and livelihoods and are experiencing severe psychological trauma. Women and girls face particularly heightened risks of sexual harassment, assault, rape, intimate partner violence (IPV), and other forms of GBV, as documented by consultations conducted by the GBV Area of Responsibility (GBV AoR).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project addresses the critical needs of these vulnerable populations by integrating Gender-Based Violence (GBV) response and prevention services with emergency shelter and economic assistance. Through a multi-sectoral approach, the project spans three key clusters: Protection - GBV, Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI), and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA). These interventions aim to enhance affected populations' safety, dignity, and resilience tonbsp58,352 people innbspthenbspKassala and Al Jazirah States. The project will be implemented in the localities of Al Jazirah (Managil and Qurashi) and Kassala (Al Girba, New Halfa, and Reifi).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe Protection - Gender-Based Violence (GBV) component is at the heart of this intervention, directly targeting 31,850 individuals with life-saving and survivor-centered services. Key activities include establishing five Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) in Kassala and Al Jazirah States, where women and girls can access psychosocial support, case management, and life skills training. The project will also distribute 4,000 dignity kits to vulnerable women and girls, ensuring their health, safety, and dignity. Additionally, 1,250 individuals, including GBV survivors, will receive tailored case management and psychosocial support. The project will also train service providers on GBV case management services, equipping them with skills to deliver survivor-centered care effectively. Community-Based Protection Networks (CBPNs) will be established to identify, refer, and address GBV cases. At the same time, awareness-raising activities will engage 16,650 individuals in GBV prevention, including targeted programs for 150 adolescent girls. GBV safety audits will also guide risk mitigation strategies in displacement settings.ltbrgtThe Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI) component will reach 3,217 households, providing essential materials such as emergency shelter kits and non-food items like blankets, mosquito nets, and solar lamps. These distributions will address immediate needs, enhance living conditions, and improve safety for displaced families. The Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) component will support 1,200 vulnerable households, enabling them to meet basic needs such as food, healthcare, and transportation. This financial support will alleviate economic stressors that increase vulnerability to GBV.ltbrgtMany of the targeted families have been displaced for over seven months, depleting their limited resources and further exacerbating their vulnerabilities. Women and girls, in particular, face heightened risks due to precarious living conditions and an inability to meet essential needs. Combining immediate humanitarian assistance with longer-term resilience-building measures, this project aims to create safer, more dignified living conditions for displaced and host communities. Continuous community feedback mechanisms and regular monitoring will ensure accountability, inform adaptive programming, and address evolving needs effectively.lt/pgt
